$comment: facts@1 (graph-store plan 0.1, T1). The fact relations circle-ir owes the store, as Arrow columns in canonical order keyed by ids@0.1 (stable-ids plan adopted 2026-11-01). The contract follows the 2026-11-01 reconciliation record (decisions 1-11) and the stable-ids decision 1a of the same evening (fixed-width node ids, so flow fills): 128-bit ids, sets with no nulls, the producer's metadata keys, hex digests. This file is the schema the store reads; the TypeScript mirror is src/facts/schema.ts and tests/facts/schema.test.ts locks the two together.

id_encoding.$comment: An ids@0.1 id is 128 bits printed as 26 lowercase base32 characters (RFC 4648, unpadded). In a column it is the 16 raw bytes, so every id column is FixedSizeBinary(16); the 2 trailing padding bits of the printed form are always zero. Node ids (the flow endpoints) have the same width: see node_id.

node_id.$comment: The fixed-width form of an ids@0.1 node id (stable-ids design decision 1a, adopted 2026-11-01): digest128 over the parts listed, i.e. BLAKE3 of the UTF-8 parts each followed by NUL, first 16 bytes - the same construction as every other ids@0.1 id, printed as 26 base32 characters where a printed form is needed. body_id is the printed body id of the innermost declaration whose body encloses the node (<decl id>.<body_hash>, 53 characters; after the snapshot's #n re-key where decl applied one); kind is the IR array the node comes from; ordinal counts the nodes of that kind inside that body in IR array order, from 0, in decimal without leading zeros. It is a function of the printed node id <body_id>/<tag><ordinal> (tags b, d, u, c) and nothing else: an edit to one body re-keys only that body's nodes. The example is a test vector (tests/facts/schema.test.ts recomputes it).

types.$comment: The closed set of column types. `dict` is Dictionary<Int8 index, Utf8 value> over a fixed vocabulary listed on the column; the whole vocabulary is written as the dictionary, in the listed order, whether or not every value occurs.

canonical_order.$comment: Within a relation rows are sorted ascending by the key columns in key order, then by every remaining column in schema order, so the comparator is total and a relation has one byte form. Column orders: fixed16 by unsigned bytes; u32 numerically; utf8 and dict by Unicode code point (which equals UTF-8 byte order), never by UTF-16 code unit or dictionary index; bool false before true; null before every value (a dead branch: no column is nullable). Relations are sets: after the sort exact duplicate rows are dropped and counted (manifest duplicates_dropped per relation), so rows are strictly increasing and a store may refuse equal rows.

chunking.$comment: After the canonical sort a relation is cut into record batches of chunk_rows rows each (the last one shorter); a relation with no rows has no record batch. One Arrow IPC file per relation, so the batch boundaries are part of the bytes. Fixed row-count chunks were chosen over the design's file_id ranges because five of the eight relations are not keyed by file_id; see the plan's open questions.

metadata.$comment: Schema-level custom metadata, and nothing else (no timestamps, no host): facts (the value facts@1, never a -draft) and ids always; engine and parser when the caller names them. The producer's manifest.json beside the files repeats them and adds source, chunk_rows and per relation file, rows, batches, bytes, blake3 (file-byte digest, hex) and duplicates_dropped.

columns.name: file_id
columns.doc: 0-based index of the file in the snapshot's path-sorted (code point order) file list; dense and per snapshot.

columns.name: content_hash
columns.doc: blake3 of the file's UTF-8 bytes, first 16 bytes.

columns.name: id
columns.doc: ids@0.1 declaration id. Unique per snapshot: when two files derive the same id (two package-info.java of one package in different bundles), the later one in file order takes the stable-ids #n suffix on its qualified_name and the id derived from it, as the ids@0.1 duplicate rule does within one scope.

columns.name: signature
columns.doc: The ids@0.1 canonical signature as written; empty for modules and types without type parameters.

columns.name: body_hash
columns.doc: ids@0.1 body hash; all-zero bytes when the engine derived none (no nulls in facts@1; Java always derives one).

columns.name: caller_id
columns.doc: The enclosing declaration (the module's id for top-level code).

columns.name: callee_id
columns.doc: The declaration that can run; one row per candidate body on polymorphic.

columns.name: method_name
columns.doc: The name as written at the site. Not in the design's column list: a (file, line, col) site names more than one call in a chained expression, and the name is what tells them apart.

unresolved.doc: Key: the site and the name as written (reconciliation row 9) plus receiver and reason, because on real data one site and name still carries several rows that differ only in those (T4, 2026-11-01). caller_id is a function of the site and not in the key.

columns.name: receiver
columns.doc: The library type the call lands on; empty when unknown (no nulls in facts@1).

flow.doc: Def-use and taint edges on ids@0.1 node ids in their fixed-width form (node_id). The java-graph@0.1 post-pass writes one def-use row per DFG use with a reaching definition in the same file: from_id = the definition's node id (kind def), to_id = the use's node id (kind use); data flows from from_id to to_id. taint rows are not written by the post-pass yet (the engine's taint flows are line-keyed, not node-keyed); the kind stays in the vocabulary for them.

columns.name: target
columns.doc: The imported name as written, without a trailing `.*`; a static import's member path for `import static`.

columns.name: wildcard
columns.doc: In the key: one file may import both X and X.*, which share target.

columns.name: kind
columns.doc: entry-index@0.1 kinds plus the design's data-declared kinds; the engine's `bean` is written as `di` (one meaning, one word).

columns.name: source
columns.doc: What declared the entry — the annotation, the supertype member, the manifest or file; the engine's evidence line.

moved.doc: Moves and renames between two snapshots: facts, not delete + insert. Empty from a single-snapshot post-pass.
